records.title: Headache and Decompression Sickness: Type I or Type II?
records.locator: Printed pp. 2-1 and 2-3, case histories and clinical archive review

record_screening.basis: Printed p. 2-3. The same counts and dates are reported in Butler et al. RTO paper 1.

case_histories.symptoms: Occipital headache during research protocol. After return to ground pressure she had nausea and focal tenderness.
case_histories.exam_and_course: Neurological examination normal. The source reports relief within 15 minutes of recompression, with no reported recurrence.

case_histories.symptoms: Left lateral orbital headache after a reportedly uneventful chamber flight.
case_histories.exam_and_course: The person did not seek evaluation. Symptoms were gone the next morning.

case_histories.symptoms: Left orbital headache recurred after a separate chamber flight on the following day.
case_histories.exam_and_course: The exam was neurologically normal, with focal discomfort and no sinus tenderness. Headache resolved after 45 minutes of oxygen without recompression.

records.note: The two numbered research histories concern two people and three exposures. Membership in the treated archive and the underlying research cohorts is unavailable. The proposed Type I classification remains a retrospective hypothesis.

observations.note: The 480 records are the same treatment cases as in Butler et al. RTO paper 1. All originally reviewed headache cases share this nested denominator.
Retrospective proposed classification required a localized headache, normal neurological examination, and rapid resolution after recompression. The estimate describes candidate reclassification.
This relaxed retrospective rule uses the normal exam alone. It includes cases meeting the stricter rule and supplies no additional cases.
